title: The Harborlight Ledger
overview: A regional charity finds a series of small payments to a newly created supplier. The transfers are individually below the normal review threshold.
objective: Trace who approved the payments and determine whether the supplier was legitimate or a vehicle for deliberate misappropriation.

hypotheses.statement: Finance director Owen Price created a shell supplier and split invoices to divert charity funds.
The payments were legitimate emergency purchases entered under a temporary supplier name.

evidence.title: Internal audit notice
evidence.content: Nine payments totaling $38,400 were made to Harborlight Services over six weeks. No active contract is listed.

evidence.title: Payment approval matrix
evidence.content: Payments below $5,000 require one finance approver. Owen Price managed supplier onboarding and routine approvals.

evidence.title: Supplier registration file
evidence.content: Harborlight Services was registered from a mailbox address. Its contact number matches a personal number listed for Owen Price.

evidence.title: Invoice pattern analysis
evidence.content: Each invoice was $4,800 or less, just below the independent review threshold. Descriptions repeat the same generic wording.

evidence.title: Program staff interviews
evidence.content: Program leads said no Harborlight Services work was requested or delivered during the payment period.

suspects.name: Owen Price
suspects.role: Finance director responsible for onboarding and approvals

suspects.name: Harborlight Services
suspects.role: New supplier with no known work history

witness_statements.statement: They did not request or receive services from Harborlight Services.

timeline.event: Harborlight Services was added as a supplier.
Nine payments were approved below the independent review threshold.
Program leads confirmed no work had been delivered.
